t: This Act may be cited as the “America’s Law Enforcement and Mental Health Project”.

fable.w: This section is only a short-title provision naming the Act. The tempting reading is that "Law Enforcement and Mental Health Project" implies collaboration with outside parties, but that is just a proper noun. The text sets up no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard short title provision. It merely establishes the name by which the Act is known and does not create any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties. There are no actors involved in a decision-making process here.
qwen_block.s: This Act may be cited as the “America’s Law Enforcement and Mental Health Project”.

opus.w: This section only gives the Act's short title. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue. Words in the title like "Project" or "Law Enforcement" don't describe any process involving people outside the federal government.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning:** One might read "Project" or "Law Enforcement and Mental Health" as pointing to a joint effort with outside groups. That reading doesn't hold up. This section is only the Act's short title. It sets up no process, and it brings no state, local, expert or public party into any federal decision.
